audits.title: 989 Improving the Completion of Hospital Anticipatory Care Plans in Orthopaedic Trauma Wards During The COVID-19 Pandemic
audits.standard: All patients admitted acutely should have a Hospital Anticipatory Care Plan (HACP) completed within 24 hours
audits.setting: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics; orthopaedic trauma wards

cycle1.result: 37/50 (74%) had HACPs completed; 18/37 (49%) completed within 24 hours; median time to completion 45.3 hours (range 0.4-275.1 hours)

audits.intervention: Staff teaching sessions and dissemination of infographic posters
audits.other_findings: Carried out during the COVID-19 pandemic; cycle 2 completion within 24 hours is not given in the supplied text.
audits.citation: McCann C, Powell-Bowns M, Duckworth A, White T. 989 Improving the Completion of Hospital Anticipatory Care Plans in Orthopaedic Trauma Wards During The COVID-19 Pandemic. Br J Surg. 2021;108(Suppl 2).

audits.title: 2254 Improving the quality and breadth of advance care planning discussions on gerontology wards in an acute London trust
audits.standard: National guidance on advance care planning

cycle1.result: Preferred place of death documented 24%; treatment escalation plan 41%; preferred place of care 59%; CPR recommendations most discussed.

audits.intervention: New ACP toolkit, training programme and electronic ACP flowsheet in the patient record system, via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Preferred place of death 60% (p 0.011); treatment escalation plan 75% (p 0.014); preferred place of care 71% (p 0.066).

audits.other_findings: Spiritual needs, information needs, prognostic discussion, broader social needs and what mattered most to the patient did not improve significantly.
audits.citation: Curtis T, Crabtree S, Al-Hashimi S, Hasan S, Osborne G. 2254 Improving the quality and breadth of advance care planning discussions on gerontology wards in an acute London trust. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae139.027.

audits.title: 142 Advance Care Planning in Patients with Dementia: An Audit on End of Life Care in Hospital Deaths
audits.standard: NICE guidance that people with dementia should have every opportunity to discuss future care wishes
audits.setting: Large tertiary referral hospital, St James's Hospital, Dublin; patients with dementia who died in hospital

cycle1.result: Only 14% had an advance care plan; 22% had resuscitation status recorded on admission; palliative care involved in 40%.

audits.other_findings: Resuscitation status was mostly documented about 15 days before death; 2 patients had no status documented and 3 received CPR.
audits.citation: Sullivan R, Power C, Greene E, Purcell R. 142 Advance Care Planning in Patients with Dementia: An Audit on End of Life Care in Hospital Deaths. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii1-iii16. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz102.29.

audits.title: Inadequate completion of advance care directives by individuals with dementia: national audit of health and aged care facilities.
audits.setting: 96 Australian hospitals, general practices and residential aged care facilities

cycle1.result: 60.8% (n=844) had ACP documentation; 31.6% (n=438) had a self-completed advance care directive; 29.3% (n=406) had ACP completed by someone else.

audits.other_findings: Self-completion was associated with age, country of birth, setting and site ACP training, policies or guidelines.
audits.citation: Bryant J, Sellars M, Sinclair C, Detering K, Buck K, Waller A, et al.. Inadequate completion of advance care directives by individuals with dementia: national audit of health and aged care facilities. BMJ Support Palliat Care. 2021. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2020-002767. PMID: 33397661.

audits.title: Advance care and resuscitation plans in a tertiary hospital: a multimodal approach.
audits.standard: Documented advance care plan before death, completed within 24 hours of admission
audits.setting: Inpatients who died at a tertiary hospital (Concord Repatriation General Hospital, Sydney)

cycle1.result: 80% had documented ACP before death; NFR documentation on admission 33%

audits.intervention: Multimodal interventions to improve ACP (not detailed)

cycle2.result: 97% had documented ACP before death; 65% of ACPs completed within 24 hours of admission

audits.other_findings: Earlier audit in 2011; in 2021, 94% had a paper resuscitation form but 64% used identification stickers and 25% were only partly completed; palliative care consulted for 44%.
audits.citation: Suresh S, Au A, Mohan S, Huang J, Guthrie C, Lee JT, et al.. Advance care and resuscitation plans in a tertiary hospital: a multimodal approach. BMJ Support Palliat Care. 2023. doi:10.1136/spcare-2023-004476. PMID: 37553202.

audits.title: Real World Implementation of the Serious Illness Care Program in Cancer Care: Results of a Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: Guidelines for early goals-of-care discussions; target at least 24 serious illness conversations with at least 95% documented
audits.setting: Two outpatient medical oncology clinics, Tom Baker Cancer Centre, Calgary

cycle1.result: Documentation rates 4.2% for clinician A and 0% for clinician B.

audits.intervention: Serious Illness Care Program, a systematic multicomponent intervention for conducting and documenting conversations.

cycle2.result: 15 conversations held, 14 (93%) documented in the EMR; documentation rates 5.4% (clinician A) and 7.3% (clinician B).

audits.other_findings: The target number of conversations was not met; further improvement cycles are needed.
audits.citation: Karim S, Lupichuk S, Tan A, Sinnarajah A, Simon J. Real World Implementation of the Serious Illness Care Program in Cancer Care: Results of a Quality Improvement Initiative. J Palliat Med. 2021;24(6):905-909. doi:10.1089/jpm.2020.0680. PMID: 33434442.

audits.title: AN AUDIT INTO ADVANCED CARE PLANNING FOR END OF LIFE CARE PATIENTS AT KINGSTON HOSPITAL
audits.standard: Local targets: resuscitation status 100%; prognosis, ceiling of care, readmission plans, patient/family awareness 95% in notes; 100% on discharge documentation
audits.setting: Care of the elderly ward, Kingston Hospital

cycle1.result: Notes: resuscitation status 82%, prognosis 55%, ceiling of care 41%, readmission plans 14%, awareness 77%. Discharge: resuscitation status 6%, ceiling of care 56%, readmission plans 33%, awareness 59%.

audits.intervention: Advance care planning summary proforma, introduced at a department meeting with teaching for junior doctors.

cycle2.result: Notes: resuscitation status 97%, prognosis 95%, ceiling of care 100%, readmission plans 100%, awareness 100%. Discharge: resuscitation status 89%, others 100%.

audits.other_findings: In cycle 1, on-call teams had to make escalation plans for 4 patients and there were 3 complaints.
audits.citation: Merrick S, Guilhem E, Kreeger L. AN AUDIT INTO ADVANCED CARE PLANNING FOR END OF LIFE CARE PATIENTS AT KINGSTON HOSPITAL. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2014;4(Suppl 1):A96.1-A96. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2014-000654.276.
